column2: Vālmīki questions Nārada about ideal man --- Nārada names Rāma of Ikṣvāku race --- Rāma honors exile and Bharata waits at Nandigrāma --- Rāma kills Khara, Triśiras, Dūṣaṇa in forest --- Rāvaṇa steals Sītā with Mārīca trick --- Rāma befriends Sugrīva and slays Vālin --- Hanumān leaps ocean and finds Sītā --- Rāma has Nala build bridge and slays Rāvaṇa --- Rāma crowns Vibhīṣaṇa and regains kingdom --- Nārada praises Rāmāyaṇa reading fruit

Vālmīki honors departing Nārada --- Vālmīki reaches Tamasā ford with Bharadvāja --- Niṣāda kills male krauñca before grieving mate --- Vālmīki curses Niṣāda in metrical ślōka --- Bharadvāja memorizes verse as Vālmīki bathes pondering --- Brahmā visits hermitage and Vālmīki worships him --- Brahmā commissions Rāma epic and promises enduring fame --- Disciples chant verse as Vālmīki resolves Rāmāyaṇa

Vālmīki sips water and meditates on Rāma's story --- Vālmīki beholds Rāma birth virtues marriage and bow breaking --- Kaikēyī blocks consecration and Rāma accepts forest exile --- Daśaratha dies lamenting and Bharata carries sandals to Nandigrāma --- Rāma roams Daṇḍaka meets sages and disfigures Śūrpaṇakhā --- Khara Triśiras and Mārīca fall and Rāvaṇa abducts Sītā --- Rāma mourns meets Kabandha Śabarī Hanumān and befriends Sugrīva --- Rāma slays Vālin and Hanumān leaps ocean finds Sītā and burns Laṅkā --- Rāma bridges ocean slays Rāvaṇa crowns Vibhīṣaṇa and returns crowned --- Vālmīki composes future deeds including Sītā exile in Uttara

Vālmīki composes Rāma's complete story as singable poem --- Vālmīki teaches the epic to Kuśa and Lava --- Kuśa and Lava sing before assembled sages --- Sages weep, praise singers, grant water jar and bark cloth --- Rāma sees singers on streets and royal roads --- Rāma brings singers home and honors them --- Rāma seats court and bids singers to sing

Narrator vows to tell Rāmāyaṇa of Ikṣvāku line --- Sagara digs ocean followed by sixty thousand sons --- Kōsala prospers on Sarayū with wealth and grain --- Manu builds famed Ayōdhyā with broad straight highways --- Daśaratha dwells in Ayōdhyā like Indra in heaven --- City shines with gates, markets, palaces, music, banners --- Expert archers and thousands of mahārathas guard city --- Vedic brāhmaṇas truthful and generous attend Daśaratha

Daśaratha guards Ayōdhyā like Manu --- Truthful king protects city like Indra guards Amarāvatī --- Citizens rest content truthful learned and generous --- None poor miserly cruel ignorant or atheist appears --- Brāhmaṇas study give sacrifice and shun excess gifts --- Four varṇas keep dharma each serving higher orders --- Fiery warriors horses and mountain elephants fill aptly named city

Daśaratha keeps eight glorious ministers --- Dhr̥ṣṭi Jayanta Vijaya Siddhārtha Arthasādhaka Aśōka Mantrapāla and Sumantra serve him --- Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadēva serve as honored priests --- Ministers speak truth, learn law, and know all plots --- They punish justly, fill treasury, and shield the innocent --- City and kingdom rest peaceful without liars or villains --- Daśaratha rules the earth and finds no equal foe --- King shines among counselors like the risen sun

Sonless Daśaratha resolves to perform horse sacrifice --- Daśaratha orders Sumantra to fetch gurus and priests --- Sumantra recalls Sanatkumāra prophecy about royal sons --- Forest sage R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga knows only father and fire --- Lōmapāda transgression brings terrible drought to Aṅga --- Brāhmaṇas prescribe fetching R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga and wedding Śāntā --- Courtesans lure sage, rain falls, Śāntā weds him --- R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga will grant Daśaratha sons --- Delighted Daśaratha asks how sage was brought

Sumantra recounts bringing of R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga --- Purōhita plans seduction by sense pleasures --- Courtesans enter forest near āśram --- R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga meets women and offers worship --- Women feed him sweets and depart in fear --- Restless sage returns next day to women --- Women lure sage to their dwelling --- Rain falls as sage travels --- King welcomes sage and weds him to Śāntā

Sanatkumāra foretells Daśaratha seeking R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga for four sons --- Sumantra urges Daśaratha to fetch sage himself with honor --- Daśaratha consults Vasiṣṭha and journeys to Lōmapāda court --- Daśaratha honors R̥ṣyaśr̥ṅga and sojourns seven-eight days --- Daśaratha requests Śāntā and husband visit his city --- Lōmapāda consents and kings part in joyful embrace --- Citizens adorn city and greet sage with drums --- Daśaratha houses sage in harem and harem honors Śāntā

Daśaratha longs for sons in spring and resolves to sacrifice --- Daśaratha propitiates R̥śyaśr̥ṅga for progeny rite --- R̥śyaśr̥ṅga assents and orders stores gathered and horse freed --- Sumantra fetches Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadēva, Jābāli, Kāśyapa, Suyajña --- Daśaratha declares childless grief and vows horse sacrifice --- Priests approve and promise four mighty sons --- Daśaratha orders stores, guarded horse, Sarayū ground, warning Brahmarākṣasas seek flaws --- Ministers obey, priests praise king and depart, king retires

Daśaratha honors Vasiṣṭha after full year and seeks offspring rite --- Vasiṣṭha agrees and summons elders, builders, artisans, learned men --- Vasiṣṭha orders bricks, royal lodges, food for all --- Vasiṣṭha commands honor for every caste without contempt or anger --- Vasiṣṭha sends Sumantra to fetch Janaka, Kāśi, Kēkaya, Lōmapāda, all kings --- Sumantra dispatches men and rides out himself to fetch kings --- Workers report readiness and kings arrive bearing gems --- Daśaratha enters ground on lucky day and priests led by R̥śyaśr̥ṅga begin rite

Daśaratha opens horse sacrifice on Sarayū bank --- Priests perform flawless rites daily --- All guests eat unstintingly from mountainous food heaps --- Eloquent priests debate between rites --- Craftsmen raise gold-adorned posts and Garuḍa altar --- Kausalyā cuts horse with three knives and keeps night vigil --- Priests burn offerings and king inhales cleansing smoke --- King gives lavish gifts after priests refuse earth --- R̥śyaśr̥ṅga promises four lineage-bearing sons

R̥śyaśr̥ṅga promises Daśaratha offspring rite --- R̥śyaśr̥ṅga begins rite and offers into fire --- Gods, Gandharvas, Siddhas and sages assemble for shares --- Gods plead with Brahmā against Rāvaṇa oppression --- Brahmā declares Rāvaṇa slayable by humans alone --- Gods rejoice at Brahmā word --- Viṣṇu arrives to join Brahmā --- Gods ask Viṣṇu to be born as Daśaratha's four sons to slay Rāvaṇa

Viṣṇu asks gods for means to kill Rāvaṇa --- Gods bid Viṣṇu take human form and slay Rāvaṇa --- Gods cite Brahmā boon sparing Rāvaṇa from all but humans --- Viṣṇu chooses Daśaratha as father --- Childless Daśaratha performs son-desiring rite --- Fire-born being emerges bearing vessel of divine payasa --- Being gives payasa for queens to eat and bear sons --- Daśaratha honors vanishing being and divides payasa among Kausalyā, Sumitrā, Kaikēyī

Brahmā orders gods to father shapeshifting monkey sons for Viṣṇu --- Gods beget vanara sons on Apsarases, Gandharvīs, Yakṣa, serpent, ape, Vidyādhara, Kiṃnara mothers --- R̥ṣis, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, serpents and Cāraṇas beget heroic forest roamers --- Thousands rise intent on killing Rāvaṇa --- Each son mirrors his divine father in form and prowess --- Stone-hurling fighters wield nails, teeth and every weapon --- Ten million troop-leaders father heroic monkeys --- Sugrīva and Vālin gather monkey hosts to aid Rāma

Horse rite ends and gods depart with shares --- Daśaratha enters Ayōdhyā and dismisses guest kings --- R̥śyaśr̥ṅga departs with Śāntā under royal escort --- Four princes are born and Vasiṣṭha names them --- Lakṣmaṇa cleaves to Rāma and Śatrughna to Bharata --- Daśaratha plans his sons' marriages --- Viśvāmitra arrives and Daśaratha offers arghya --- Daśaratha pledges to grant any wish

Viśvāmitra praises Daśaratha and claims promised help --- Mārīca and Subāhu drench altar with flesh and blood --- Viśvāmitra quits rite barred from anger and curse --- Viśvāmitra demands young Rāma for ten nights --- Viśvāmitra promises Rāma divine guard and world fame --- Viśvāmitra declares only Rāma can kill demons --- Viśvāmitra seeks Vasiṣṭha-led counsel approval --- Daśaratha hears plea and shakes with fear

Daśaratha revives after stunned moment and replies --- He calls Rāma under sixteen unfit to fight Rākṣasas --- He offers his full army and his own bow for protection --- He says moment apart kills him, pleads age and hard-won love --- He asks Rākṣasas' strength, parentage, size, remedy --- Viśvāmitra names Rāvaṇa, Brahmā-booned son of Viśravas, scourge of worlds --- He says Rāvaṇa sends Mārīca and Subāhu to spoil sacrifice --- Daśaratha says even gods cannot endure Rāvaṇa in battle --- Daśaratha withholds untrained boy but offers himself to fight

Viśvāmitra rebukes Daśaratha for breaking his promise --- Viśvāmitra threatens to depart and leave king with kin --- Earth shakes and fear enters gods at his wrath --- Vasiṣṭha urges Daśaratha to keep promise and uphold dharma --- Vasiṣṭha declares Rākṣasas cannot harm Rāma guarded by Viśvāmitra --- Vasiṣṭha praises Viśvāmitra as embodied dharma knowing all weapons --- Kr̥śāśva sons come as fifty weapons from Jayā and fifty Saṃhāras from Suprabhā --- Vasiṣṭha bids king send Rāma without doubt

Daśaratha joyfully summons Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa --- Mother father and Vasiṣṭha bless Rāma with rites --- Daśaratha kisses head and gives son to Viśvāmitra --- Flowers rain and drums sound at departure --- Viśvāmitra leads armed Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa forth --- Viśvāmitra grants Balā and Atibalā lore at Sarayū --- Balā and Atibalā bar hunger fatigue demons and grant peerless fame --- Rāma sips water receiving lore and trio spends happy night on Sarayū bank

Viśvāmitra wakes sleeping Rāma for dawn rites --- Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa bathe chant and greet sage --- Trio reaches auspicious Gaṅgā Sarayū confluence --- Princes ask whose holy āśrama stands there --- Viśvāmitra tells how Śiva burned impudent Kāma bodiless --- Fallen limb names Aṅga land disciples keep sinless āśrama --- Trio lodges between rivers to cross tomorrow --- Sages welcome trio with offerings stories and rest

Sages offer boat urging Viśvāmitra onward crossing river with both princes --- Rāma asks about tumultuous midstream water roar --- Viśvāmitra explains Sarayū born from Brahmā Mānasa lake --- Princes salute Gaṅgā meeting and gain southern bank --- Rāma asks whose dread beast-filled forest this is --- Viśvāmitra tells Indra cleansed stain founded Malada Karūṣa --- Viśvāmitra describes Tāṭakā ravaging both fertile districts --- Viśvāmitra orders Rāma to kill Tāṭakā and free country

Rāma asks how frail yakṣa woman holds thousand-elephant strength --- Viśvāmitra credits Brahmā boon for her might --- Sukētu wins daughter Tāṭakā and elephant strength through tapas --- Tāṭakā weds Sunda and bears Mārīca --- Widowed Tāṭakā assaults Agastya with son --- Agastya curses Mārīca to rākṣasa-hood and Tāṭakā to man-eating ugliness --- Enraged Tāṭakā ravages Agastya land --- Viśvāmitra bids Rāma kill her guiltless citing Śakra and Viṣṇu precedents

Rāma vows to obey father and Viśvāmitra by slaying Tāṭakā --- Rāma draws bow filling quarters with bowstring twang --- Tāṭakā rushes raging toward the sound --- Rāma shows demoness to Lakṣmaṇa vowing to cripple her --- Tāṭakā raises arms roaring charging Rāma --- Rāma fells Tāṭakā with chest arrow --- Gods praise Rāma bidding Viśvāmitra gift divine weapons --- Gods depart as evening falls Viśvāmitra kisses Rāma bidding camp for night

Viśvāmitra passes night then praises Rāma --- Viśvāmitra offers all divine weapons for victory --- Viśvāmitra names cakras, thunderbolt, nooses, maces and missiles --- Rāma receives mantra lore facing east --- Weapons approach Rāma as servants --- Rāma accepts weapons by touch and thought --- Rāma salutes Viśvāmitra and prepares to depart

Rāma asks Viśvāmitra for weapon withdrawals --- Viśvāmitra teaches withdrawal lore of Kr̥śāśva sons --- Radiant weapons appear embodied before Rāma --- Weapons offer service with folded hands --- Rāma sends weapons to await mental summons --- Weapons circumambulate Rāma before departing --- Rāma admires deer-filled bird-gladdened grove --- Rāma asks whose hermitage wicked killers have reached

Rāma asks about forest --- Viśvāmitra names Siddhāśrama as Vāmana home --- Bali defeats gods and rules three worlds --- Gods beg Viṣṇu to check sacrificer Bali --- Viṣṇu takes dwarf birth and wins three strides --- Viṣṇu restores triple world to Indra --- Viśvāmitra claims hermitage and brings Rāma to kill demons --- Sages honor guests, princes urge rite and keep vigil

Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa ask Viśvāmitra for attack moment --- Sages order six-night sleepless guard during silence vow --- Princes guard penance grove without sleep for six nights --- On sixth day Rāma alerts Lakṣmaṇa as sacrifice blazes and sky roars --- Mārīca Subāhu and followers rush raining blood streams --- Rāma hurls Mānava weapon casting Mārīca hundred yojanas oceanward --- Rāma shows Lakṣmaṇa spared senseless whirling Mārīca --- Rāma fells Subāhu with Āgnēya and followers with Vāyavya --- Sages honor Rāma like Indra as Viśvāmitra declares Siddhāśrama fulfilled

Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa spend night content in Siddhāśrama --- Brothers greet Viśvāmitra at dawn and offer service --- Sages invite princes to Janaka Mithilā sacrifice --- Sages describe unstringable divine bow sought by failed kings --- Host leaves Siddhāśrama with carts, beasts and birds following --- Party camps on Śōṇā bank and worships evening fire --- Rāma asks about rich forest land, Viśvāmitra begins tale

Kuśa fathers four sons by Vaidarbhī and bids them rule --- Four sons found Kauśāmbī Mahōdaya Dharmāraṇya Girivraja --- Viśvāmitra shows Vasu land of five hills and Māgadhī river --- Kuśanābha fathers hundred daughters by Ghr̥tācī --- Maidens sing dance and play in garden --- Vāyu demands maidens wed him for long life --- Maidens refuse Vāyu and uphold father choice --- Angry Vāyu cripples maidens reaching palace as king questions them

Hundred maidens tell Kuśanābha how Vāyu crippled them --- Kuśanābha praises daughters' united forgiveness --- Kuśanābha consults ministers on wedding daughters --- Sōmadā serves ascetic Cūlin and earns boon --- Cūlin grants unwed Sōmadā mind-born son Brahmadatta --- Kuśanābha weds hundred daughters to Brahmadatta --- Hand touch straightens hunchbacked brides into radiance --- Kuśanābha sends couples off while Sōmadā welcomes brides

Kuśa promises childless Kuśanābha a son Gādhi --- Kuśa returns to Brahmalōka --- Gādhi fathers Viśvāmitra and Satyavatī --- Satyavatī weds R̥cīka and becomes Kauśikī river --- Viśvāmitra leaves Kauśikī for Siddhāśrama --- Viśvāmitra marks midnight and urges Rāma to sleep --- Moon rises and flesh-eaters roam abroad --- Sages applaud Viśvāmitra --- Rāma praises sage and sleeps

Viśvāmitra wakes Rāma at dawn on Śōṇa bank --- Rāma performs morning rites and asks crossing path --- Viśvāmitra shows R̥ṣi path and leads party onward --- Party reaches Jāhnavī at midday and camps rejoicing --- Party bathes, offers oblations and gathers round Viśvāmitra --- Rāma asks how Gaṅgā traverses three worlds to ocean --- Viśvāmitra names Mēnā's peerless daughters Gaṅgā and Umā --- Gods take Gaṅgā for three worlds and Himavat weds Umā to Rudra

Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa praise Viśvāmitra and seek Gaṅgā triple-path story --- Śiva pursues union with Umā for a hundred divine years without issue --- Alarmed gods beg Śiva to restrain his unbearable brilliance --- Śiva discharges his displaced brilliance upon the earth --- Agni enters the brilliance with wind and forms White Mountain --- Kārtikēya is born of fire, gods worship Śiva and Umā --- Wrathful Umā curses divine wives to barrenness and earth to many lords --- Śiva withdraws with Umā to a Himalayan peak for austerities

Gods ask Brahmā for commander --- Brahmā names Gaṅgā and Agni as parents --- Gods appoint Agni to beget son --- Agni floods Gaṅgā with burning tējas --- Gaṅgā pleads unable to bear tējas --- Gaṅgā casts embryo forming gold, metals and golden forest --- Kr̥ttikās nurse six-faced Kumāra as shared son --- Gods name him Skanda Kārtikēya and anoint commander after conquering Daitya hosts

Viśvāmitra begins Sagara tale for Rāma --- Childless Sagara performs tapas with two wives at Himavat --- Bhr̥gu grants progeny and fame boon after century --- Kēśinī takes single heir, Sumati takes sixty thousand --- Sagara honors Bhr̥gu and returns home with wives --- Kēśinī bears Asamañja, Sumati bears gourd brood --- Nurses raise sixty thousand sons in ghee jars --- Asamañja drowns children in Sarayū and faces exile --- Aṃśumān wins love of whole world --- Sagara resolves to perform sacrifice with priests

Rāma asks Viśvāmitra for Sagara sacrifice in full --- Viśvāmitra tells of Sagara rite between Himavat and Vindhya --- Aṃśumān guards horse while Indra steals it in Rākṣasa form --- Priests urge Sagara to recover horse and save rite --- Sagara sends sixty thousand sons digging while he waits initiated --- Sons cleave Jambudvīpa to Rasātala slaying beings --- Terrified gods tell Brahmā sons dig earth and slay creatures

Brahmā reassures gods Kapila bears earth and foretells sons doom --- Delighted gods return home --- Earth breaks with thunderous crash --- Sagara sons report failure to find horse and seek counsel --- Sagara orders renewed digging to seize thief --- Sons honor Virūpākṣa in east and Mahāpadma in south --- Sons honor Saumanasa in west and Bhadra in north --- Sons dig northeast and find Kapila with grazing horse --- Sons accuse Kapila and charge shouting halt --- Kapila utters Huṃkāra and burns sons to ashes

Sagara sends Aṃśumān to trace fathers and horse-thief --- Aṃśumān takes bow and sword down fathers path --- Aṃśumān questions direction-elephants and wins blessing --- Aṃśumān finds ash-heaped fathers and laments slaying --- Aṃśumān finds sacrificial horse grazing nearby --- Garuḍa tells Kapila burnt fathers, Gaṅgā alone frees them --- Aṃśumān returns horse and reports Garuḍa words --- Sagara completes sacrifice, rules thirty thousand years and dies

People crown Aṃśumant king after Sagara dies --- Aṃśumant grants Dilīpa kingdom and practises fierce tapas on Himavat --- Aṃśumant wins heaven after thirty-two thousand years --- Dilīpa grieves for burnt forefathers and finds no rescue --- Dilīpa crowns Bhagīratha and dies of sickness --- Bhagīratha performs fierce penance at Gōkarṇa for thousand years --- Brahmā comes with gods and offers Bhagīratha boon --- Bhagīratha asks Gaṅgā water for Sagara sons and heir --- Brahmā grants boon and bids Bhagīratha win Śiva to hold Gaṅgā

Bhagīratha worships standing on toe tip for year --- Śiva promises to bear mountain daughter on head --- Gaṅgā takes huge form and falls onto Śiva head --- Gaṅgā wanders trapped in tangled locks for years --- Śiva releases Gaṅgā toward Bindu lake --- Gods crowd sky to watch Gaṅgā fall --- Falling waters twist, flash and shine pure --- Cursed bathers turn pure and regain their worlds --- Bhagīratha leads in chariot while gods and creatures follow Gaṅgā

Bhagīratha leads Gaṅgā to ash-filled ocean pit --- Gaṅgā floods ashes with her waters --- Brahmā declares sixty thousand Sagaras heaven-bound --- Brahmā names Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī Tripathagā and daughter --- Brahmā exalts Bhagīratha above Sagara Aṃśumant Dilīpa --- Brahmā enjoins bath and rites and leaves for heaven --- Bhagīratha completes rites and rules joyfully in capital --- Viśvāmitra closes tale and notes evening

Rāma marvels at Viśvāmitra narration and ponders overnight with Lakṣmaṇa --- At dawn Rāma boards waiting boat and crosses Gaṅgā --- Party reaches north bank and beholds splendid Viśālā city --- Rāma asks Viśvāmitra which dynasty rules Viśālā --- Viśvāmitra tells gods churning ocean with Vāsuki and Mandara --- Dhanvantari and sixty-crore Apsarases arise unclaimed and stay common --- Vāruṇī arises and gods claim her while demons refuse her --- Uccaiḥśravas, Kaustubha, and Amr̥ta arise; gods slay demons and Indra rules

Diti mourns slain sons and asks Kāśyapa for Indra-slaying son --- Kāśyapa promises son if she stays pure thousand years --- Kāśyapa blesses Diti and leaves for tapas --- Diti performs fierce tapas at Kuśaplavana as Indra serves offerings --- Diti promises Indra brother and shared conquest in ten years --- Diti sleeps at midday impure with feet at head --- Indra enters womb and splits wailing fetus sevenfold with vajra --- Diti forbids killing and Indra emerges begging forgiveness

Diti asks Indra to make forty-nine sons wind-roaming Maruts --- Indra grants boon with folded hands --- Diti and sons ascend to heaven fulfilled --- Viśvāmitra names land as Indra dwelling serving Diti --- Viśvāmitra recites Viśālā kings from Viśāla to Sumati --- Viśvāmitra declares night halt before visiting Janaka --- Sumati welcomes Viśvāmitra with honors and homage

Sumati asks Viśvāmitra about two armed princes --- Viśvāmitra recounts Siddhāśrama stay and Rākṣasa slaying --- Sumati honors Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as guests overnight --- Princes depart for Mithilā as sages applaud Mithilā --- Rāma notices empty hermitage and asks its history --- Viśvāmitra names it Gautama āśrama shared with Ahalyā --- Indra in sage disguise seduces consenting Ahalyā --- Gautama catches fleeing Indra and curses away his testicles --- Gautama dooms Ahalyā invisible until Rāma frees her and leaves for Himālaya

Indra begs gods to restore his lost testicles --- Gods bid Pitr̥dēvas give ram testicles to Indra --- Pitr̥dēvas fit ram testicles onto thousand-eyed Indra --- Viśvāmitra leads Rāma to redeem radiant Ahalyā --- Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa enter Gautama hermitage and behold Ahalyā --- Princes grasp Ahalyā feet and accept her hospitality --- Gods rain flowers and praise purified Ahalyā --- Gautama reunites with Ahalyā and honors Rāma --- Rāma receives honor and departs for Mithilā

Rāma Lakṣmaṇa and Viśvāmitra reach Janaka sacrifice ground --- Viśvāmitra camps party on secluded watered ground --- Janaka honors Viśvāmitra with priestly arghya --- Janaka seats sages and declares sacrifice fruitful --- Janaka says twelve days remain and bids Viśvāmitra stay --- Janaka asks who two armed godlike youths are --- Viśvāmitra names Daśaratha sons and recounts their journey

Śatānanda marvels seeing Rāma --- Śatānanda questions Viśvāmitra about Ahalyā worshipping Rāma and rejoining Gautama --- Viśvāmitra confirms Ahalyā reunites with Gautama like Rēṇukā --- Śatānanda welcomes Rāma, praises Viśvāmitra as protector --- Śatānanda recites Viśvāmitra lineage from Kuśa to Gādhi --- Śatānanda describes Viśvāmitra long righteous reign, earth tour --- Viśvāmitra beholds Vasiṣṭha hermitage thronged by ascetics, celestials

Viśvāmitra bows to Vasiṣṭha --- Vasiṣṭha seats him and offers fruits and roots --- Both ask mutual welfare and talk gladly --- Vasiṣṭha offers feast to Viśvāmitra and army --- Viśvāmitra declines and seeks leave --- Vasiṣṭha presses invitation again and again --- Viśvāmitra yields and Vasiṣṭha summons Śabalā for feast

Śabalā creates food and drink for every desire --- Vasiṣṭha feasts Viśvāmitra's army to contentment --- Viśvāmitra asks Śabalā for a hundred thousand cows --- Viśvāmitra claims kings rightfully take jewels --- Vasiṣṭha refuses cows, crores and silver heaps --- Vasiṣṭha says rites, offerings and livelihood rest on her --- Viśvāmitra offers elephants, chariots, horses and crore cows --- Vasiṣṭha refuses to yield his wish-granting cow

Viśvāmitra drags Śabalā away --- Śabalā laments abandonment weeping --- Śabalā shakes off servants and reaches Vasiṣṭha feet --- Vasiṣṭha denies abandonment, calls king stronger with full army --- Śabalā declares brāhmaṇa power beats Kṣatriya and seeks commission --- Vasiṣṭha bids Śabalā create foe-crushing force --- Śabalā bellows Pahlavas destroying Viśvāmitra army --- Viśvāmitra destroys Pahlavas with weapons --- Śabalā creates Śaka-Yavana host burning his army --- Viśvāmitra looses mighty missiles

Vasiṣṭha orders Śabalā to create troops by yōga --- Śabalā births Kāmbōjas, Pahlavas, Yavanas, Śakas, Mēcchas, Hārītas, Kirātas --- Hosts destroy Viśvāmitra's army with horses, elephants and chariots --- Viśvāmitra's hundred sons rush Vasiṣṭha with many weapons --- Vasiṣṭha burns the hundred sons to ash with huṃkāra --- Humiliated Viśvāmitra crowns one son and seeks Himālaya tapas --- Śiva grants Viśvāmitra Dhanurvēda and all divine weapons --- Armed Viśvāmitra burns the grove and scatters sages and beasts --- Vasiṣṭha reassures fearful and raises death-staff cursing Viśvāmitra

Viśvāmitra hurls Āgnēya weapon and cries stand --- Vasiṣṭha stands firm and mocks Kṣatriya strength --- Vasiṣṭha quenches the fire weapon with Brahmadaṇḍa --- Viśvāmitra hurls scores of divine weapons --- Vasiṣṭha swallows every weapon with his staff --- Viśvāmitra looses Brahmāstra and terrifies three worlds --- Vasiṣṭha swallows Brahmāstra and blazes with fire from every pore --- Sages praise Vasiṣṭha and he calms his wrath --- Humbled Viśvāmitra scorns Kṣatriya might and vows tapas for brāhmaṇhood

Humbled Viśvāmitra sighs over Vasiṣṭha defeat --- Viśvāmitra retires south with wife and practices fierce root-fruit tapas --- Righteous sons Haviṣpanda, Madhuṣpanda, Dr̥ḍhanētra, Mahāratha are born --- Brahmā names Viśvāmitra rājar̥ṣi after thousand years and departs --- Shamed Viśvāmitra deems tapas fruitless and resumes fiercer tapas --- Triśaṅku resolves to sacrifice and reach heaven in body --- Vasiṣṭha declares rite impossible and rejects Triśaṅku --- Triśaṅku finds hundred Vasiṣṭha sons and begs bodily-heaven sacrifice

Vasiṣṭha sons rebuke Triśaṅku for bypassing guru --- Vasiṣṭha sons refuse his rite and send him home --- Triśaṅku vows to seek another refuge --- Enraged sons curse Triśaṅku into caṇḍāla form --- Ministers and citizens abandon transformed king and flee --- Lonely burning king seeks Viśvāmitra --- Compassionate Viśvāmitra asks his errand --- Triśaṅku pleads bodily heaven and begs fate reversed

Viśvāmitra welcomes caṇḍāla-formed Triśaṅku and promises refuge --- Viśvāmitra vows Triśaṅku shall reach heaven bodily --- Viśvāmitra orders sons to gather sacrifice stores --- Viśvāmitra sends disciples to summon sages from all lands --- Disciples report Vasiṣṭhas refuse and mock caṇḍāla sacrifice --- Viśvāmitra curses Vasiṣṭhas to seven hundred Muṣṭika dog-meat births --- Viśvāmitra dooms Mahōdaya to Niṣāda outcast life

Lakṣmaṇa continues Vr̥tra aftermath for Rāma --- Sense-stripped Indra cowers at world end like coiled snake --- Earth withers drought-stricken without thousand-eyed Indra --- Gods carry Aśvamēdha rite to hiding Indra --- Gods complete great horse rite to cleanse Indra --- Brahmahatyā demands lodging and gods quarter her fourfold --- Brahmahatyā lodges in rivers, trees, women and brāhmaṇa-slayers --- Purified Indra rises feverless and the world calms --- Lakṣmaṇa urges Rāma to perform same Aśvamēdha

Rāma approves Lakṣmaṇa and begins King Ila tale --- Righteous Ila rules earth and hunts spring forest --- Hunting Ila nears Śiva grove where males turn female --- Woman-formed Śiva sports with Umā and attendants --- Ila with retinue turns female and despairs --- Ilā surrenders to laughing Śiva seeking manhood --- Śiva denies manhood and offers another boon --- Ilā worships Umā who grants shared half-boon --- Ila chooses alternate months forgetting other sex

Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata marvel and ask Ilā fate --- Rāma resumes tale at curious brothers bidding --- Woman Ilā roams forest woods with female retinue --- Ilā abandons vehicles and sports in mountain hollow --- Ilā finds Budha blazing in lake waters --- Ilā churns whole lake with former male followers --- Love-struck Budha emerges and questions four women --- Women call Ilā their masterless mistress roaming woods --- Budha divines Ilā truth and settles followers as Kiṃpuruṣīs

Rāma resumes Ila tale for wondering Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata --- Budha loves consenting masterless Ilā and enjoys Mādhava month --- Man-formed Ila wakes and asks Budha for missing army --- Budha claims hailstorm slew servants and Ila slept sheltered --- Grieving Ila vows to yield kingdom to son Śaśabindu --- Budha consoles Ila and bids him dwell a year --- Ila dwells alternating womanly delight and manly duty --- Ilā bears Purūravas in ninth month and gives child to Budha --- Budha comforts man-formed king with righteous tales

Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata ask Ila fate --- Rāma begins Prajāpati-son tale --- Budha summons Saṃvarta and other savants --- Kardama prescribes Śiva horse sacrifice --- Sages perform great rite near Budha āśrama --- Pleased Rudra restores Ila manhood and vanishes --- Ila founds famed Pratiṣṭhāna in Madhyadēśa --- Ila attains Brahmalōka and Purūravas succeeds him --- Rāma extols horse rite restoring manhood

Rāma tells Lakṣmaṇa of horse rite resolve --- Rāma summons Vasiṣṭha and chief brāhmaṇas --- Brāhmaṇas bless Rāma after hearing plan --- Rāma orders invitations to Sugrīva and monkeys --- Rāma invites Vibhīṣaṇa and rākṣasas --- Rāma invites kings, brāhmaṇas, and sages with wives --- Rāma fixes Naimiṣa ground on Gōmatī --- Rāma sends Bharata ahead with grain and gold --- Rāma orders shops, artisans, mothers, and golden wife brought

Rāma releases spotted horse under Lakṣmaṇa guard --- Rāma reaches Naimiṣa and rejoices at ground --- Kings arrive and Rāma honors them with lodgings --- Bharata and Śatrughna supply food and garments --- Monkeys serve brāhmaṇas and Vibhīṣaṇa serves sages --- Monkeys and rākṣasas give freely to beggars --- Sages marvel at endless gold, gems, and garments --- Year-long flawless rite continues unabated

Vālmīki arrives with pupils during rite --- Vālmīki builds secluded huts near r̥ṣi lodgings --- Vālmīki bids pupils sing whole Rāmāyaṇa everywhere --- Vālmīki names streets, homes, Rāma door, and priests --- Vālmīki offers mountain fruits and roots for strength --- Vālmīki orders twenty sargas daily without greed --- Vālmīki tells boys to claim themselves as his pupils --- Vālmīki demands sweet tuned singing honoring king --- Boys memorize words and sleep eagerly

Boys bathe and sing as taught --- Rāma hears unprecedented song and marvels --- Rāma gathers sages, kings, scholars, and elders --- Crowd deems boys mirror images of Rāma --- Boys sing twenty sargas from Nārada vision --- Rāma offers eighteen thousand gold through Bharata --- Boys refuse gold as forest fruit-eaters --- Rāma asks poem extent and author --- Boys name Vālmīki and five hundred sargas --- Rāma agrees to hear more and boys withdraw

Rāma recognizes singers as Sītā sons --- Rāma sends envoys with word to Vālmīki --- Rāma asks sinless Sītā to swear for his cleansing --- Envoys bow and deliver soft sweet message --- Vālmīki consents to please Rāma --- Envoys report muni word to Rāma --- Rāma invites all to witness Sītā oath --- Sages and kings applaud and praise Rāma --- Rāma fixes tomorrow and dismisses assembly

Rāma summons sages, kings, monkeys, and rākṣasas --- Thousands gather to watch Sītā oath --- Vālmīki arrives swiftly with lowered-eyed Sītā --- Crowd hails pair amid grief and tumult --- Vālmīki enters crowd and addresses Rāma --- Vālmīki declares Sītā virtuous and sinlessly abandoned --- Vālmīki swears twin boys are Rāma sons --- Vālmīki stakes tapas fruit on Sītā purity

Rāma folds hands and trusts Vālmīki word --- Rāma admits abandoning known-sinless Sītā from fear --- Rāma owns twin sons and seeks love for Maithilī --- Gods led by Brahmā gather in sky --- Sweet wind delights watching crowd --- Sītā vows sole devotion and seeks earth cleft --- Earth throne rises borne by mighty serpents --- Earth goddess seats Sītā and she enters Rasātala --- Flowers rain and gods cry approval --- Beings stare stunned at Rāma and Sītā

Rāma deems world empty without Vaidehī --- Rāma dismisses kings, bears, monkeys, rākṣasas, and enriched brāhmaṇas --- Rāma returns to Ayōdhyā brooding on Sītā --- Rāma keeps golden Jānakī for rites and takes no wife --- Rāma sacrifices ten thousand years with full fees --- Rāma rules in dharma with loyal bears, monkeys, rākṣasas, and kings --- Rain falls timely and none dies untimely --- Rāma mothers die and join Daśaratha in heaven --- Rāma gives ancestral gifts honoring mothers and Pitr̥s

Yudhājit sends Gārgya with horses and gifts --- Rāma meets and honors uncle envoy --- Rāma asks uncle message --- Gārgya describes Gandharva land on Sindhu banks --- Gārgya urges conquest and two cities --- Rāma assigns Bharata sons Takṣa and Puṣkala --- Rāma orders Bharata-led slaughter and settlement --- Rāma consecrates lads and sends army forth --- Beasts, rākṣasas, and birds follow bloodthirsty host --- Army marches six weeks and reaches Kēkaya

Yudhājit welcomes arriving Bharata with joy --- Bharata and Yudhājit reach Gandharva city with army --- Gandharvas roar and seek battle on every side --- Armies fight dreadful seven-night battle without decision --- Enraged Bharata looses dreadful Saṃvarta weapon of Kāla --- Weapon fells three crores Gandharvas in an instant --- Bharata founds Takṣaśilā for Takṣa and Puṣkarāvatī for Puṣkara --- Bharata dwells five years and returns to Ayōdhyā pleasing Rāma

Rāma deems Aṅgada and Candrakētu worthy of kingdoms --- Rāma seeks pleasant land harming no king or āśrama --- Bharata proposes healthy Kārāpatha for both cities --- Rāma founds Aṅgadīyā and heavenly Candrakāntā in Malla land --- Princes are consecrated and dispatched west and north with armies --- Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata escort sons one year and return to Rāma --- Brothers serve Rāma in dharma for ten thousand years

Kāla approaches palace gate as ascetic --- Ascetic asks Lakṣmaṇa to announce urgent mission --- Lakṣmaṇa swiftly informs Rāma of ascetic --- Rāma welcomes sunlike messenger and offers worship --- Ascetic demands private talk with death for seer-hearer --- Rāma vows secrecy and posts Lakṣmaṇa at door --- Rāma dismisses doorkeeper and invites ascetic to speak

Kāla claims Brahmā sent him to Rāma --- Kāla declares himself all-destroying Kāla born of Māyā --- Kāla recalls Viṣṇu forming earth from Madhu Kaiṭabha bones --- Kāla recalls Viṣṇu creating Brahmā on lotus for creation work --- Kāla recalls Rāma taking humanity to kill Rāvaṇa --- Kāla announces fixed ten thousand years now complete --- Brahmā offers continued rule or Viṣṇu heaven with gods --- Rāma laughs and agrees to return whence he came

Durvāsas seeks instant audience at palace gate --- Durvāsas orders Lakṣmaṇa to announce him immediately --- Lakṣmaṇa asks sage to wait for busy Rāma --- Enraged Durvāsas threatens to curse city Rāma Bharata progeny --- Lakṣmaṇa accepts own death and informs Rāma --- Rāma dismisses Kāla and honors Durvāsas --- Durvāsas seeks ready food ending thousand-year fast --- Rāma serves food and grieves remembering Kāla after sage departs

Lakṣmaṇa finds Rāma downcast like eclipsed moon --- Lakṣmaṇa urges Rāma to kill him without grief --- Lakṣmaṇa warns promise-breakers enter hell --- Rāma consults ministers and family priest Vasiṣṭha --- Vasiṣṭha foresees ruin in separation from Lakṣmaṇa --- Vasiṣṭha orders abandonment to preserve dharma and worlds --- Rāma renounces Lakṣmaṇa as equal to death --- Lakṣmaṇa restrains breath at Sarayū without entering home --- Gods shower flowers and Indra bears Lakṣmaṇa bodily to heaven

Grief-stricken Rāma vows to crown Bharata and follow Lakṣmaṇa --- Subjects fall senseless and Bharata faints --- Bharata swears he wants no kingdom without Rāma --- Bharata proposes crowning Kuśa in Kōsala and Lava in north --- Bharata urges swift messengers to Śatrughna --- Vasiṣṭha bids Rāma heed devoted subjects --- Subjects vow to follow Rāma with wives and children --- Rāma crowns Kuśa and Lava and sends messengers to Śatrughna

Messengers reach Mathurā in three days without halting --- Messengers report Lakṣmaṇa loss Rāma vow sons crowning citizens following --- Messengers name Kuśāvatī for Kuśa Śrāvatī for Lava and lonely Ayōdhyā --- Śatrughna hears dreaded ruin and summons subjects and priest --- Śatrughna tells all and his resolve with brothers --- Śatrughna crowns Subāhu at Mathurā and Śatrughātin at Vaidīśa --- Śatrughna divides Mādhurī army with wealth grain between kings --- Śatrughna rushes alone to Ayōdhyā and bows to blazing Rāma --- Śatrughna declares consecrated sons and resolve to follow Rāma --- Vanaras seek to follow, Vibhīṣaṇa stays in Laṅkā, Hanumān lives, rest may follow Rāma

Rāma bids Agnihōtra fire and Vājapēya umbrella lead highway --- Vasiṣṭha performs lawful great-departure rite completely --- Rāma grasps Kuśa reciting Brahma and leaves house silent motionless --- Śrī Hrī Resolve weapons in human form follow Rāma --- Vēdāḥ Sāvitrī Ōṅkāra Vaṣaṭkāra in brahmin form follow Rāma --- Sages queens servants Bharata Śatrughna follow Rāma --- Brahmins with fires families ministers subjects follow rejoicing --- Countrymen bears monkeys demons follow devotedly without sorrow

Rāma reaches holy Sarayū after half yōjana --- Brahmā arrives with gods sages in divine vimānas --- Flowers rain as Rāma steps into Sarayū water --- Brahmā bids Viṣṇu enter eternal body with brothers --- Rāma with brothers enters Vaiṣṇava glory bodily --- Gods worship Viṣṇu-arrived god with joy --- Viṣṇu seeks worlds for loving self-abandoning followers --- Brahmā grants Sāntānika worlds and Brahma-near abode to animals --- Monkeys bears regain divine origins and all bathe attaining heaven --- Brahmā sends all heavenward and departs with gods
